data.exact_reserve_text: Included within claims notified of USD 1,547.3m (2022: USD 1,398.0m) is a decrease in claims notified relating to 2022 and prior years of account of USD 54.6m (2022: decrease in claims notified relating to 2021 and prior years of account of USD 229.9m).

prior_year_events.event_name: Loss Portfolio Reinsurance (LPR) with another Lloyd's syndicate
prior_year_events.impact_description: Indemnified against potential adverse development in respect of net liabilities, providing protection in several professional lines portfolios predominantly relating to 2019 and prior years of account.

prior_year_events.event_name: Reinsurance to Close of Syndicate 2007 and Syndicate 6129 into 2019 year of Syndicate 1686
prior_year_events.impact_description: RITC transaction concluded the business of both Syndicate 6129 and Syndicate 2007; the financial impact of this transaction is nil.

named_events.loss_description: The war and related impacts are a risk tracked from an underwriting and reserving perspective; exposures are described as low and containable and the Syndicate is minimising exposure to Russian business.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2023 was USD 2,113.637m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates a net prior-year strengthening of approximately USD 116.166m (5.5% of opening gross reserves), driven by adverse development across several older underwriting years partially offset by favourable movements in notified claims (a reported USD 54.6m decrease relating to 2022 and prior). Key influences include reinsurance arrangements (notably the 2022 LPR covering professional lines), IBNR recalibration and evolving litigation and inflationary pressures affecting reserving assumptions.
raw_causal_phrases: decrease in claims notified relating to 2022 and prior years of account of USD 54.6m
indemnified against potential adverse development in respect of net liabilities
Reserves for losses and loss expenses are calculated in accordance with actuarial practice based on substantiated assumptions, methods and assessments.
changes in the law, differences in loss adjustment practice, medical and long-term care, and economic factors such as inflation can have a considerable impact on run-off results
data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Note 4 'Provision for claims outstanding' (gross) at 1 Jan 2023. Prior-year development derived from the gross claims development table (claims triangle) by comparing the latest estimate to the prior diagonal for underwriting years 2014-2021 and summing the changes (triangle in USD '000 was converted to millions). The report contains references to a 2022 LPR and a 2021 RITC which can distort movements; the LPR affected reinsurance recoveries in 2022 and may affect net but not directly the gross triangle. Some narrative prior-year movements quoted in the text are net of reinsurance; where no explicit gross prior-year movement was provided, the triangle was used. All monetary amounts are reported in the report's native currency (USD) and expressed in millions.
